chats.answer:
For keeping a chest freezer running through a 3-day (72-hour) power outage, I recommend a portable power station with at least 3–4 kWh of battery capacity, preferably expandable to 6 kWh or more.

Yes, solar panels can make a big difference. With sufficient sunlight, they can extend your backup from three days to potentially much longer.

The key is that a chest freezer doesn't run continuously. Its compressor cycles on and off, so its total daily energy consumption matters much more than its running wattage.

A 2 kWh station might last three days with a very efficient freezer, but a 4 kWh station provides much more breathing room.

Illustrative estimates, not a weather forecast

A 400 W solar array could approximately offset the freezer's daily consumption on a reasonably sunny day. Cloud cover, shade, season, and panel placement can substantially reduce output.

For reliable three-day protection, I would choose a 4 kWh battery plus 400–800 W of solar panels. That provides a useful combination of stored energy for nighttime or cloudy weather and daytime recharging.

One important step before buying

Measure your freezer's consumption for 24–48 hours using a plug-in energy meter, or check its EnergyGuide label. Also confirm the power station can handle the compressor's startup surge. For a freezer-only setup, spending more for very high inverter wattage usually isn't necessary.
